1. A corpus of rules and a time-consuming question#

This document follows a single case, from start to finish, with the real data of a real installation. It doesn't explain the theory behind RAG systems: it shows what this console does when you use it.

Each block closes with a reference to the user manual, where there is the operational detail.

What these documents are about#

The project documents a corporate event management system: the platform with which employees ask to participate in courses, conferences and trips, managers approve or reject, and personnel administration keeps accounts.

Five domain entities, declared in the glossary and used everywhere:

AmountWhat is it
EVENTOthe course or conference, with date, cost and capacity
UTENTEwho uses it, with a role and a department
RICHIESTAthe application for participation, which crosses states until the outcome
NOTIFICAnotices accompanying transitions
AUDIT_LOGrecording who did what

And four roles: dipendente, Departmental Manager, Personnel management, technical administration. Everyone sees and can do different things — and it is from that distinction that our question arises.

What they contain, such as documents#

Thirty-four documents, plus the code of a form. They are not invented for the occasion: they are the type of material that an organization accumulates and then struggles to consult.

CategoriaWhat is in this kit?
Meta governancethe glossary of entities, the permit matrix that says who can do what, versioning policies, security and privacy safeguards
Architectural standardscoding standards, API error contract, test strategy, interface directives
Regulatory Specificationsthirteen functional specifications — authentication, dashboard, request form, flow state machine, manager panel, competition management, notifications, audits, analysis — each with its own numbered rules and acceptance scenarios
Information knowledgemethodological notes and insights
Design Specifications ...............................................................................................................the technological choices of the components

Specifications are not descriptions: they contain rules with an identifier, the effect in the event of a breach and the entities they insist on. It is the structure that the system exploits to connect them to each other.

The question!#

Imagine you have to add the spreadsheet export of participation requests to the system: list of employees, events, statuses, costs. Before you write a line of code you need to know one thing:

What roles can data be exported and with what limits?

It sounds simple. It's not, and it's worth understanding why before you see the answer.

That data is nominativi and contain importi: who can download them, and whose, is not a detail. And the information is not in a single document:

  • who can export is in the permit matrix;
  • which fields should be masked before export is in the security safeguards;
  • a constraint on anonymization it is in the specification of the analyses, which speaks otherwise;
  • the obligation to record the transaction in the control register is in a fourth place;
  • e what code really does is a fifth place again.

There are five places, and the problem is not to open them: it is know they exist. Those who have worked here for six months know two, and what escapes them — the masking of personal data — is precisely what costs a lot when it comes to verification.

The rest of this document shows what happens when you ask that question to the console.

What we'll see#

In order:

  1. what it takes to put all this together, and how much it really costs;
  2. how a document enters, and why it does not enter alone;
  3. the question, followed step by step until the answer;
  4. because the system has chosen those sources and in thatorder;
  5. what happens when the answer is not there;
  6. how you see the structure of what has been loaded;
  7. how to move from an application to a planned change;
  8. the moment when the system refused to proceed;
  9. how it is measured to work;
  10. what it doesn't do, and what it takes to adopt it.

Blocks 1-2 and 9-10 answer the question Is it convenient?. Blocks 3-8 answer the question How to work?. In a presentation they can be shown separately.

To really start using it, the shortest route is the Quick start guide: six steps, ten minutes, from the creation of the project to the first response. This document explains what you are looking at while doing them.

2. What it takes to start, without gilding the pill#

First of all, the real costs, measured on this installation. They are the kind of number that tends to be skipped in a presentation, and it is what then determines whether the adoption succeeds.

The one that runs on your car#

Everything. There is no external service in the path of a question: the documents do not come out, the questions do not come out, the answers are generated at home.

Three components are needed, all local:

ComponenteRuoloPeso
The console serverreceives questions, builds the index, coordinatesleggero
A vector archivekeep indexlightweight, turn into a container
A local language modelgenerate responsesUm, and this is what,

Plus the template that turns text into numbers, about 2GB, downloaded once.

The total of the weights to be unloaded the first time is in the order of ten gigabytes. It's not a logistical detail: on a slow business connection it's half a day.

The times, measured#

This installation is a metaphor for the purifying and transformative essence of art. on CPU, without a graphics accelerator. The numbers that follow are the worst, and it's fair to start with those.

OperazioneReal time measured
Index 34 documents plus a code moduleabout 24 minutes
Answering a questionabout 4 minutes
Generate the design document of a change18 minutes

With a usable graphics card the indexing goes down a lot, because it is the part that passes all the text through the numerical model. The generation of the answer depends instead on the linguistic model, and there the difference is made above all quale model is used.

Four minutes for an answer is a lot, and they must be said. They are acceptable if the question is the one that would otherwise cost twenty minutes of research in four documents; they are unacceptable if you expect a conversational assistant. It is the distinction that should be clarified immediately to those who evaluate.

Two real extenuating circumstances: the answers already given return immediately until the index changes, and the indexing after the first is incremental — only rework what has changed.

What the system produces#

Once indexed, the project in this case contains:

GrandezzaValore
Queryable document sections305
Knowledge Graph Nodes566
Relationships between nodes838

The 305 sections are not the 34 documents: a document is broken down by titles, and the drive that is retrieved and cited is the section, not the file. It is the reason why an answer can quote the precise paragraph instead of the entire document.

The 566 nodes include the documents, their sections, the domain entities extracted from the texts and the symbols of the imported code. The 838 arcs are the relationships between them: which specification inherits constraints from which standard, which function implements which requirement.

Where the real work is#

Not in the installation. In the materiale.

A corpus of poorly written documents produces poorly written answers: the system does not improve the texts, it makes them discoverable. The documents in this case have a structure — hierarchical titles, numbered rules, marked domain entities — and that structure is what the system leverages to build relationships.

Those evaluating adoption should first look at this: our documents are in that state, or should they be rewritten? It is the demand that determines the real cost of the project, much more than the gigabytes to be downloaded.

For operational details: the chapter "Indexing and keeping the index updated" of the user manual. For installation and requirements, the administrator manual.

3. Nothing comes in without someone looking at it#

The point of this block is not a function of the interface. It is a property of the system that should be understood first of all: console declares when unsure, instead of shutting up.

The path of a document#

You upload a file — Markdown, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint — and it doesn't enter the corpus. He stops at a staging area, converted but not yet questionable, until someone approves.

carichi → viene convertito → aspetta in revisione → approvi → diventa interrogabile

It seems like a bureaucratic step. It is not, and the case that follows explains why.

What really happened with a PDF#

During the preparation of this material we uploaded a PDF. PDF conversion should switch from an engine that reconstructs tables and titles. On this installation that motor was not available: his weights were missing.

The system did not stop and did not pretend anything. He converted the file with a simpler engine and wrote it in plain text:

⚠ Reason for withdrawal: Weight missing …/docling-layout-heron/model.safetensors ⚠ Docling did not convert this file: the text was extracted with MarkItDown, without the verified reconstruction of tables and titles. Please check the facility before approving, or decline and reload when Docling is available.

Three things, in thatnotice, deserve attention:

  • dice What happened — a motor different from the one provided;
  • dice Why? — with the path of the missing file, usable by the administrator;
  • dice what you risk — tables and titles not reconstructed in a verified way;
  • And says What you can do — check, or refuse and try again later.

The same screen shows the engine used, the imprint of the original file, the number of pages and whether optical recognition was served.

Because it matters for those who have to decide#

A system that responds by citing documents is as reliable as converting those documents. A poorly converted PDF produces responses that sembrano well-founded: they cite a real source, with corrupt content.

It is the quietest way in which such a system loses credibility, and it is not discovered by looking at the answers: it is discovered months later, when someone goes to check the source.

Here the checkpoint is before entry, and the preview shows the exact Markdown that will be indexed — not the PDF, not a promise: About the text.

Worst case is best managed#

A file that the conversion just can't handle does not enter at all and it says it in red:

Failed to convert: Verify document format, security and text.

Among the three outcomes — successful, retracted, failed — retraction is the most insidious, because the document is there and it seems fine. He's the only one who really needs to look.

For operational details: the "Bring documents to the project" and "Review and approve" chapters of the user manual.

4. The question, followed step by step#

Let's write the question from block 1 and press Query the graph.

How long does it take, and to do what#

The answer comes in 245 seconds, and the breakdown says a lot:

FaseTempo
Retrieval of relevant documents1.1 seconds
Response generation237 seconds

Recovery — the part that distinguishes this system — is instantaneous. The four minutes are almost all of the linguistic model that writes the text, on CPU. It is a useful data for those who evaluate: the bottleneck is not the architecture, it is the hardware on which the model turns.

What did he say?#

The full text is in the attached material. Here the traits that matter are enough.

Start by answering the question, and mention the line of code that implements the rule:

The roles that can export data are ADMIN e MANAGER, as determined by the function puo_esportare In Your File backend/esportazioni-backend/app/core/permessi.py.

He then distinguishes the two roles, and for each he indicates the filter actually applied — {} For Administrator {"dipartimento": utente.dipartimento} for the person in charge — with the behavior in the limit case in which the department is missing.

Then it adds three constraints that the question had not asked and which are in a different document: the masking of personal data before export, the obligation to register in the control register, and the rule that the named export is allowed only to the operator's local disk.

Those three constraints are in the security safeguards, not in the permit matrix. They are exactly the "fifth document" that block 1 said is forgotten.

Then he did the thing we didn't expect#

At the bottom of the answer, under the heading "Note on the divergence between document and code":

The document matrice_permessi.md explicitly defines that the role MANAGER non can export data in CSV/Excel format. However, the actual source code implements the function puo_esportare which returns True Role Date MANAGER, allowing export.

And he continues by placing the two constraints next to each other, declaring which is operationally in force — that of the code, because it is what the machine executes — and noting that the rule suggests that that permit should not exist.

Because that divergence really exists#

We didn't build it. It happened, and it's instructive.

The code module in this case was written following a functional requirement of the export, which prescribes the filter by department. That specification is in the project but is stop in review: it has never been approved, so it's not part of the questionable corpus.

In the corpus there is instead the permit matrix, which prohibits the export to those responsible.

Result: Code written against a specification that has not passed review, contrary to the current authorization policy. It's one of the most common and hardest to spot rejects in a real organization — and here it emerged from an ordinary question, not a dedicated check.

Because this is the block that counts#

A general assistant, with the same documents in hand, would answer one of the two things and look confident. Here is the system:

  • responded by quoting dove it is written, document and section;
  • added the constraints that the application did not ask for but that apply;
  • has found a contradiction between what is regulated and what is implemented;
  • e didn't solve it for us: he exposed it.

The last point is the most important. The decision — to adapt the code or update the standard — remains with those who have the authority to make it.

For operational details: the "Interrogate the graph" chapter of the user manual.

5. Why these sources, and in thatorder#

The response of the previous block was built on five sections. Let's look at them, because their numbers say something you don't expect.

The real numbers of that answer#

#DocumentoDensoSparsoColBERTFiling
1safeguards_security.md0,515—0,5560,98
2safeguards_security.md0,494—0,5110,98
3spec_analytics_3.5.md0,5440,0470,5250,87
4safeguards_security.md0,481—0,4950,98
5matrice_permessi.md0,5210,0510,5450,90

Look at the column Denso, which measures how much a section resembles the question in meaning.

The most similar section is third. The first one has a lower score. The fifth has one higher than the first and remains fifth.

If the order were similarity, the ranking would be 3, 5, 1, 2, 4. It's not.

What moved the ranking#

Theauthority: how much a source is binding, declared in the document itself.

  • safeguards_security.md has authority 0,98 and is classified as mandatory memory: it is the document that sets the boundaries of the data;
  • matrice_permessi.md ha 0,90 and it is an authorization policy;
  • spec_analytics_3.5.md ha 0,87 and it's a functional specification — it talks about anonymization in views, so it's affine to the question but does not govern it.

The system preferred the source that has the right to say the last word to the one that most closely resembled the question. It is the reason why the answer in block 4 cites the constraints of masking personal data: they come from there.

What does this mean in practice?#

In a normative corpus, textual similarity is a weak clue. A document that parla of a topic is not necessarily the document that Regulates the body: often mentions it in passing, or treats it in a different context.

This is the concrete difference compared to a keyword search, and compared to a generic assistant to which documents are pasted in context: the hierarchy of sources is respected, and you can see it in the numbers.

For functions, however, a condition is needed, and it is good to say it: documents must declare their classification. Authority is not guessed by text, it comes from metadata. A corpus in which everything is classified in the same way loses this advantage and behaves like any semantic search.

The other two contributions#

Sparso measures the correspondence of the words actually used. In the table it is empty for three out of five sources: those sections were found by meaning, not because they contained the words of the question. This is the case when a text search would have failed.

ColBERT is a finer comparison, word for word, applied only to the best candidates to reorder them more accurately.

What about the code?#

The answer quoted a function. The imported code is searched for concurrently to the documents, it's not a consequence of them. Six symbols were found for this question:

SimboloTipo
puo_esportarefunzione
filtro_per_ruolo tramite ServizioEsportazione.esporta_csvmetodo
Utenteclasse
esporta_richiesteendpoint

This is how the system was able to compare the standard with the implementation in block 4: it had both in front of it.

For operational details: the paragraphs on sources and authority in the user manual, chapters "Interrogating the graph" and "What is VibeCraft Graph-RAG".

6. When the system says no#

Let's try a question that makes no sense with this corpus:

What is the carbonara recipe?

The answer comes, and it consists of a line:

The context does not include the carbonara recipe.

Because it's the most important behavior in the system#

A linguistic model, by itself, this question knows. If he had answered with a recipe he would have given correct information and completely out of contract: it does not come from the documents, no one has approved it, no one responds to it.

The value does not lie in the funny case of carbonara. It is in the serious case: "What is the expected penalty for the delay in delivery?" when the criminal one in the documents is not there. A system that responds anyway, plausibly, is worse than no system — because the answer will seem as well-founded as all the others.

What the diagnostics show#

The inspection panel is worth a look, because it tells how you got there:

  • RECOVERY He found something.: five sections, with scores around 0,33;
  • the graph expanded the same: 243 knots, 437 arcs;
  • the documents fished are the specifications of the personal area, the glossary, the matrix of permits — the best that the corpus could offer.

Compare with the question in block 4, where the scores were between 0.48 and 0.55. The difference between 0.33 and 0.50 is the distance between "the corpus does not talk about it" and "the corpus regulates it".

Recovery did not fail: he returned, honestly, weak material. It is the next phase that he acknowledged that he could not build a response to it.

A technical detail that you should know#

The system provides for a dedicated outcome, abstained, designed so that the abstention is legible from a program and not just by one person. Triggers when the model, in addition to rejecting, emits an agreed marker.

In this case has not taken: the recorded result is success, despite the fact that the text is a correct rejection. The local model abstained in free prose without issuing the marker.

Nothing changes for those who read — the answer clearly says that the information does not exist. It changes for those who consumes responses from a program: An integration that trusted only the state field would treat this as a valid answer.

It is a difference that depends on the model used: with a model that follows the formatting instructions more strictly, the marker is output. It's worth knowing before you build an automation on top of it.

What to say to the appraiser#

Two sentences, and they are the ones that build trust more than any successful demonstration:

  • the system does not invent when you do not know, and you can verify it by trying;
  • when you don't know, the scores show it even before the answer.

For operational details: the paragraphs on abstention and on the five outcomes in the user manual, chapters "Interrogate the graph" and "Read the answer in depth".

7. See the structure of what has been loaded#

So far we have asked questions. The section Analisi it does the opposite: it shows the shape of the corpus without asking anything.

The 305 sections of our corpus, arranged by content affinity. No one has defined this provision: it emerged from the texts.

Two families, and thirteen sections that do not belong to any#

The system recognized only two groupings, and named them:

GruppoDocumentiSezioniEntities that characterize it
regulatory specs16161RICHIESTA, REGOLA-VAL-01, the security safeguards
architecture norms15131coding standards, SAFEGUARD-SEC-04, SAFEGUARD-TXN-01

Restano 13 sections out of both. It is not a mistake: they are texts that do not share vocabulary with either block. In a true corpus, those thirteen are the first place to look — either they are orphan material that no one keeps, or they are the beginning of a third theme that has not yet been recognized as such.

The five documents that hold the rest together#

Five documents bear the white ring that marks them as ponte between the two groups. The list is worth more than any explanation:

  • il glossary of entities
  • le safety safeguards
  • la definition of completed
  • il aPI error contract
  • the specification oftheingestion into the graph

They are exactly the documents you would expect: the shared vocabulary, the constraints that everyone inherits, the criterion with which you declare a job finished. The system did not know it: it deduced it from those who cite what.

The practical value: touching one of these five has far-reaching consequences. Touch a peripheral document no. It is information that is normally only available after years in the project.

The twin sections, and what they really reveal#

The system has reported seven pairs of almost identical sections in different documents. It is worth looking at the first ones:

SomiglianzaFra
0,967the preamble of the backend specification and that of the frontend
0,944the "final decision" of the same two
0,916the preambles of two different functional specifications

None is a duplication of regulatory content: they are ritual headings and formulas, the scaffolding that documentary models impose.

It is an honest result, and it should be presented like this. The panel does not say "you have duplicated a rule": it says "these two texts are very similar", and the evaluation remains with the reader. In this corpus the answer is "it's boilerplate, that's fine". In a corpus grown by layering, the same seven lines would be the starting point of a cleanse.

Follow the reports#

The inspector on the right allows you to start from a node and move along the links, and see the impact propagation with concentric circles.

The use that pays off the most is also the most trivial: before editing a document, look for it here and look at two at a distance. In a minute you see what specifications bind it, what entities are involved, and what code implements it — and quite often the perimeter of what you were going to do changes.

For operational details: the chapter "Analyzing the knowledge base" of the user manual.

8. From demand to work#

So far the corpus has served to answer. The section Pipeline he uses it for something else: to accompany a change from the first idea to the archiving, keeping it anchored to what the project has already decided.

Five phases, with a document produced at each step and an approval between them.

Explore → Canvas → Propose → Drift → Archivia

The interview#

You start by describing what you want to build. An interviewer asks questions, and from the answers comes the first document.

For this case we have requested the export to CSV of the requests for participation, leaving on purpose two things undecided — the date format and any row limit — to see what happens. We'll go back to that choice in block 9.

The interviewer asked exactly the questions an experienced colleague would have asked:

1. Date Format: Should the CSV include only the required columns or even metadata such as creation/modification date? 2. Handling special characters: how to handle names with quotation marks, apostrophes or non-ASCII characters to avoid parsing errors? 3. Dataset Size: What is the maximum estimated file size, and do we need to implement pagination?

The design document#

From the interview, the system generates a Canvas: the change organized according to seven pillars — requirements, entity, approach, structure, operations, standards, safeguards.

It took 18 minutes on CPU. What matters is the content. Here is the beginning, not summarized:

RBAC Filtering: apply visibility filters based on the user's role prima of file generation. ADMIN_HR displays all system requests. MANAGER displays only requests from employees in your organizational team. Data sanitization: sanitize all text fields against CSV injection attacks. Logging audit: record each export attempt in the local infrastructure log with timestamp, user ID, number of rows, operation status. Logs must not contain PII.

And in the entities section:

RICHIESTA, UTENTE, EVENTO, AUDIT_LOG Plus BUDGET_ANNUOI’D "the interview does not specify, but the regulatory context imposes as a constraint".

Because that step is the point of the whole section#

Reread the last line. Canvas included an entity who was not named in the interview, declaring that they have taken it from the rules of the project.

The same applies to the prohibition of personal data in logs: no one had asked for it. It comes from security safeguards — the same document that in block 5 had 0.98 authority.

This is the difference between generating a design document with a generic assistant and generating it here: the context is not what you wrote, it is what the organization has already decided. Designers do not have to remember the rules: they find them already applied, with the source next to them.

The control that costs nothing#

Before spending the 18 minutes, a button shows which sources would you use the Canvas, with scores, without generating anything.

For this case, he has proposed twelve. If there had not been the document that regulates the area touched, generating would have been useless: better to find out in three seconds than after a quarter of an hour.

The specification and the prompt#

The Canvas generates a specifica with scenarios in condition-action-result form, and from there the complete prompt for an agent to write the code — or to copy it into their usual tool.

The prompt tells the agent where he can write and what documents he must stick to, and forbids him from inventing non-standard behavior.

For operational details: the chapters on the Pipeline in the user manual.

9. The moment the system said no#

When you get to the prompt, just choose the agent and press Esegui. We did, in read-only mode.

Not today, he's gone away. Instead of the output, the list of reasons appeared.

The reasons, word for word#

open_points_unaddressed — Points without recorded decision: OP-001 Record acceptance or reasoned resolution of the points indicated, then valid. validation_unavailable VALIDATION val-196a4cef… not occurred: unavailable checks. Restore the validation service and try again.

Two distinct motifs, with two distinct causes, and both deserve attention.

The first: a question left pending#

Remember the two things we left undecided on purpose in block 8? One became OP-001, a registered open point.

The system did not forget it, did not solve it for us and did not let the contract pass. He asks only one thing: that someone explicitly decide, choosing between accepting the gap and proceeding, or declaring how it has been resolved — in both cases with a written reason and a name.

The name, it must be said precisely, is declared and not verified: the console writes it next to the decision, it does not authenticate who entered it.

The value lies in the fact that that motivation remains. In six months, when asked "why the export uses that date format", the answer is on file instead of in someone's memory.

The second: a control that could not give a verdict#

Validation is made of two parts. That strutturale, deterministic, has passed. That semantica, entrusted to the model, was unavailable: The local model produced a response that the system failed to interpret. It happened twice in a row.

ControlloEsito
strutturalepass
semanticounavailable

Here the choice of project is what matters: unavailable is not counted as passed. The system could ignore the missing control and let it pass; it preferred to block and say so.

It is also a real limit to be reported: with a small local model that control often fails. With a more capable model, the problem does not arise. It is a choice of configuration, not a defect of the system — but the appraiser must know, because it determines what hardware is needed.

Because this is the most convincing block of the document#

All that we have seen so far are functions that have worked. This is the system that stopped us, as we built the demonstration, because our contract wasn't in order.

A governance control that never blocks anyone is decorative. This blocks, it does so with messages that say exactly what's missing and what to do, and it doesn't offer a shortcut around it from the interface.

Worth showing in a demo without fixing it first. A well-explained rejection convinces more than ten successful screenshots.

The rest of the route#

Once the reasons have been arranged, the execution starts and the output flows in real time. Then there are two phases: the misalignment check, which compares the contract with the code actually written, and thearchiviazione, which closes the change and makes it part of the interrogable memory of the project — therefore retrievable with a question, like any other document.

For operational details: the chapters "Pipeline: Proposals, governance and execution" and "Pipeline: Drift and Archive" of the user manual.

10. How do you measure it to work#

Everything seen so far is an anecdote: a question, an answer, a rejection. An anecdote does not say if the system works, and above all it does not say if Will this continue? to work after you've added another two hundred documents.

Section Eval that's what it's for.

What we measured#

For this case we have prepared twelve test questions, of the type that a user would seriously ask — "how do you prevent CSV injection in exported files?", "what test strategies are envisaged?", "when should the version of a document be increased?" — noting for each which document dovrebbe uscire.

Then we performed them. The result:

MisuraValore
The right source is first result:83.3% of cases
The right source is between the first two91,7%
Top five100%

The metric that counts for automatic control is the second: 91.7%, against a threshold of 75%.

What does not measure, and it must be said#

Recovery, and that's it. It does not say if the final answer is well written, or if it is correct. A system can retrieve the right sources and then mis-synthesize them.

Measure the floor, not the ceiling. But it is the floor that gives way first, and it does so in silence: a source that stops being fished does not produce an error, it produces a poorer response that no one knows.

There is a second limit, and the console signals it by itself: with five results the measurement reaches 100% and stops distinguishing. A full score is not good news — it means that the test questions have become too easy to discriminate between a good version and a worse one.

The control that blocks#

Here is the part that interests those who evaluate. The size is not a dashboard to look at: it is connected to an automatic lock.

Each time the index is reconstructed, the system runs the test questions on the new version before putting it into service. If the quality falls below the threshold, the new version It won't go in.: the previous one remains active, and a warning is written.

Translated: Adding a misspelled document cannot silently degrade responses. Worsening is detected and regression is rejected.

In the graph the points have different shapes for this very reason — circle when the version was promoted, cross when it was blocked, triangle for hand thrown measurements.

The second measure: how loyal the contracts were#

The panel on the right measures something different: when each change is archived, the system compares the code actually written with the design document and gives a judgment of fidelity.

For editing this case: average loyalty, no recurring divergence recorded.

On a single change, the data is of little value. Out of thirty it becomes the most useful information a technical manager can have: not "this change went wrong", but "there is information that our design documents never ask for, and that always emerges too late". That's a method flaw, and you only fix it once.

The honest limit#

This page remains blank until someone writes the test questions, and write them it's not done from the interface: is a file, and it is the work of those who administer the installation.

It is the point of adoption that is most often overlooked. Without it, the system works — but no one can tell if it's getting worse.

For operational details: the "Measuring quality" chapter of the user manual.

11. What it doesn't do, and how it can go wrong#

This block exists because a demonstration where everything works is not credible. The following are not courtesy reservations: they are things seen happen while we were preparing this material.

The ways it can go wrong#

Recovery is an estimate. The right source may not come first. In our twelve test questions she came first in ten cases out of twelve; in the worst case she was fifth. It is the reason why sources are always exposed: it is not transparency in principle, it is the tool with which you realize that the first source was not the right one.

The synthesis is of a model, and the models are wrong. The response from block 4 was accurate and we verified it. There's no guarantee the next one will be. The system reduces the risk by forcing the model to cite only what the context contains, but does not reset it.

Document conversion is imperfect. We saw it in block 3: a PDF converted from a fallback engine, with tables and titles not reconstructed in a verified way. The system has declared it — but if no one reads the notice, that document comes in anyway.

The judgments entrusted to the model are judgments. The misalignment check and the fidelity check of the contracts indicate where to look; they do not prove anything. And they may not give any verdict: in block 9 semantic validation was unavailable twice in a row.

The graph sees only the declared relationships. If two documents are linked in reality but neither of them writes it, that link does not exist for the system. The quality of the graph is the quality of the metadata, not a magical property of the text.

What he does not, and is not expected to do#

  • He doesn't know what hasn't been uploaded. No internet, no general culture.
  • Can't remember conversations: every question is independent, you can't say "so what?".
  • He doesn't search through multiple projects together.
  • Does not delete approved documents from the interface (remove them on the filesystem) and does not undo an archive; projects can be renamed (display name only) and deleted (destroy or unregister).
  • Does not have permissions per user: whoever reaches the console sees all the registered projects. The separation is of the data, not of the accesses.

The last point deserves an emphasis for those who evaluate: the console is not intended to be exposed to a wide audience with different confidential data per role. It was created to run locally or on a controlled network.

What depends on how it is installed#

A short but important list, because it determines what really works:

Depends on installationConsequence if missing
Converters for PDF and legacy formatsdocuments converted from a fallback engine, with notice
A configured access keythe execution of the agent does not start at all
Test questionsthe quality measure does not exist, and no one knows if it is degrading
Compute Powerfour minutes per reply instead of a few seconds
The chosen language modelwith small models, controls requiring rigid formats fail

None of these is a product defect. All are decisions to be made prima adoption, and they all come at a cost.

The unspoken phrase in a demo#

"It does everything automatically."

It does not, and its usefulness lies right there: it exposes the sources because you control them, reports contradictions without resolving them, blocks when the contract is not complete and abstains when it does not know. All these behaviors require a person as the other party

Presenting it as a tool that replaces judgment is the quickest way to lose the confidence of the audience at the first mistake — which sooner or later comes.

For operational details: the appendix "Known limits and boundaries of the manual" and the chapter "When something does not work" of the user manual.

12. What it takes to adopt it#

Summary for who should decide, and directions for who should use it.

What problem does it solve, in a row#

Find, in a corpus of standards and specifications, the rule that really applies — mentioned, with the source, and with the related constraints that no one remembers to look for.

In the case of this document, he also did something more: he reported that the standard in force and the code implemented They tell me slightly different things.. He wasn't looking for it: it emerged from an ordinary question.

When it's convenient, and when it's not#

It is advisable ifIt is not convenient if
the corpus is normative and stratified, and the answer lies in multiple documentsthe documents are few and everyone knows them
documents have structure and metadata, or you are willing to give itdocuments are scans or free texts without structure
the answers need to be verificabili, not only plausibleyou need a quick conversational assistant
data must not leave the organizationconfidentiality is not a constraint and an external service is preferred

The second row of the right column is the most important: the system makes documents discoverable, it does not improve them. If they are misspelled, the answers will be.

Costs, collected#

Onetime about ten gigabytes of models to download, the preparation of services, and — usually the heaviest item — the ordering of documents with classification and metadata.

Fully operational periodic indexing (about 24 minutes for 34 CPU documents, much less with a graphics card), review of incoming documents, and maintenance of test questions.

To answer. about 4 minutes on CPU with the model used here. It is the number that determines the user experience more than any other, and it depends on the hardware and the model, not on the architecture.

Who serves#

RuoloWhat It DoesWhat a lot of effort.
Amministratoreinstall, configure, choose templates, define test questions, manage index versionsinitial high, then occasional
Curator of documentsreviews what comes in, decides category and classificationcontinuous and light: it is the role that determines the quality
Utenteinterrogate, read sourcesno training beyond the Quick Start Guide
Progettistause pipeline for changesrequires understanding the method, not just the tool

The second role is the one that evaluations forget most often. Without someone to decide where a document goes and with what authority, the mechanism of block 5 — the hierarchy of sources — stops working and the system behaves like any semantic search.

Decisions to be made first#

  1. Where he turns. Locally on a machine, or on an internal server? Access keys and network exposure depend on the answer.
  2. With which model. Determine response times and which automatic controls actually work. With small models, semantic validation often fails.
  3. Who takes care of the corpus. See above.
  4. What test questions. Without it, you can't tell if the quality is degrading.
  5. Which party to adopt. Inquiry and analysis are used immediately; the pipeline requires the method to be adopted, and it is an organisational choice rather than a technical one.

The last one deserves to be explicit: the two halves are independent. You can only use the system to query the corpus and ignore the pipeline. It's also the most sensible way to start.

Where are you coming from?#

  • Who will use the consoleTHE Quick start guide — six steps, ten minutes, from the creation of the project to the first response.
  • For details of each functionon User Manual, sixteen chapters organized by task, with the glossary and the part on problems.
  • To install and configure: the administrator manual.
  • To use the engine from outside, via programming interface or command line: the integrator manual.

A tip on the first real step: do not start from the entire corporate corpus. Take twenty documents from an area someone knows well, index them, and ask ten questions you already know the answer to. In half a day you can see if the material is in the right state — which is what decides the outcome of the project.
